text: A 57-rider breakaway seized control from the gun, and Mauro Schmid proved the strongest in the final kilometers, outdueling Tejada in a two-up sprint to claim the stage. The escape held throughout the hilly terrain, keeping the GC contenders largely neutralized—Pogačar emerged unscathed and holds his narrow three-minute cushion over Vingegaard, while Evenepoel sits third at four minutes back. The real battle looms ahead: with the Vosges mountains on deck, Vingegaard desperately needs to make his move this weekend or risk ceding ground to a UAE team that has spent four years patching every crack in Pogačar's armor.
